intro: Georgia walked into Tuscaloosa and walked out No. 1, making it official that the Bulldogs are the class of college football. Meanwhile, the Eagles blew up their offensive line in the same week, shipping out Jurgens and losing Lane Johnson for good.

stories.headline: Rays Sweep Yankees Into the Offseason, Judge Watches From the Couch
stories.body: Tampa Bay ousted New York in the ALDS to reach the ALCS for just the third time in franchise history, with Drew Rasmussen carrying a no-hitter into the eighth inning of Game 1 and striking out 10. Aaron Judge, sidelined by a calf injury, missed the entire postseason and is already lobbying the Yankees to go 'all-in' for 2027 — which is one way to process elimination.

stories.headline: Brewers Draw First Blood Against the Dodgers in Battle of the NL's Best
stories.body: Milwaukee beat Los Angeles 2–1 in NLCS Game 1 on a go-ahead fifth-inning single from Luis Lara, setting up what should be a legitimate battle between the NL's two winningest teams at 103 and 100 victories. The Dodgers, making their third straight NLCS appearance, handed the Game 1 ball to Tarik Skubal ahead of Yoshinobu Yamamoto, and it didn't go their way.

stories.headline: Guardians Claw Back From 2–0 Down, Ramirez Snaps Out of It Just in Time
stories.body: Cleveland erased a 2–0 series deficit against the White Sox, forcing and winning a decisive Game 5 to advance to the ALCS. José Ramírez shook off a batting slump with a big Game 3 performance — because of course he did.

stories.headline: Eagles Blow Up Their Offensive Line: Jurgens Traded, Lane Johnson Done
stories.body: Philadelphia shipped two-time Pro Bowl center Cam Jurgens to Baltimore for a 2028 second-rounder, then watched Lane Johnson walk away from the game after 14 years. Losing your center and your franchise tackle in the same week is a rough way to spend an October.

stories.headline: Lamar Jackson's Ankle Has Ravens Sweating Heading Into Week 5
stories.body: Jackson left the Tennessee game at halftime with an ankle injury, with Tyler Huntley stepping in and his Week 5 status listed as a long shot. Baltimore just traded for a Pro Bowl center and may now be starting a backup quarterback — great timing.

stories.headline: Barkley, Surtain, Pittman, Thornton: The NFL's Walking Wounded Pile Up
stories.body: Saquon Barkley is week-to-week with a hamstring, Patrick Surtain II tweaked his ankle in Denver's loss to San Francisco, Michael Pittman heads to IR for at least four games, and Tyquan Thornton suffered a major injury on a Raiders tackle. It's only Week 5 and the injury report is already reading like a MASH unit.

stories.headline: Georgia Walks Into Tuscaloosa and Walks Out No. 1
stories.body: The Bulldogs beat Alabama 20–17 on the road, their first regular-season win over the Tide since 2007, and jumped straight to the top of the AP Top 25. Texas also lost to Oklahoma on a last-second field goal the same week, so the entire top of the CFP picture reshuffled in 48 hours.

stories.headline: Kentucky Does the Unthinkable Twice in a Row
stories.body: The Wildcats beat No. 10 LSU 35–34 by converting a two-point play in overtime — their second straight one-point OT win, reportedly a first in FBS history. Nobody asked Kentucky to carry the SEC chaos torch, but here we are.

stories.headline: Florida Flips Five-Star Receiver Royal Right Out of Texas's Hands
stories.body: The Gators landed top-2027 wide receiver prospect Royal, who had been committed to Texas, in one of the bigger recruiting flips of the cycle so far. Texas is having quite the week.

stories.headline: Hellebuyck Goes Full Holdout, Jets Drop the Hammer
stories.body: Winnipeg goaltender Connor Hellebuyck demanded a trade, skipped training camp entirely, and got himself suspended indefinitely for the trouble. Meanwhile, Dylan Larkin is doing the polite Canadian version of the same thing in Detroit — requesting a trade but still showing up to work.

stories.headline: Oilers and Penguins Can't Stop Trading With Each Other
stories.body: Edmonton sent defenseman Spencer Stastney to Pittsburgh in exchange for forward Filip Hallander on October 7 — the second consecutive year these two clubs have pulled off an in-season swap. At this point just give them each other's front office numbers and call it a partnership.

stories.headline: Edvinsson Wants Out of Toronto and Everyone's Talking About It
stories.body: Simon Edvinsson's trade request from the Maple Leafs was one of the most-read NHL stories of the week, which says a lot about how the Leafs manage their roster situations. Toronto: still must-watch television, just not always for the right reasons.

stories.headline: Detroit Goes All-In: Duren and Ausar Thompson Get $355 Million in Extensions
stories.body: The Pistons locked up Jalen Duren on a five-year, $200 million deal and Ausar Thompson on a five-year, $155 million extension in the same week, making it a very expensive few days in Detroit. Rebuilds are cute until the bills arrive.

stories.headline: Knicks Lose Hukporti to Ruptured Achilles Before the Season Even Starts
stories.body: Ariel Hukporti ruptured his right Achilles in New York's preseason opener, adding another frontcourt headache to a team that really didn't need one. Nothing like a brutal injury in a game that doesn't count.

stories.headline: Kuminga Turns Down Lakers, Takes Short-Term Timberwolves Deal to Bet on Himself
stories.body: Jonathan Kuminga passed on a Lakers offer worth more than $12 million annually and signed a shorter deal with Minnesota, keeping himself in position to hit free agency again next summer. High-risk move, but the math makes sense if he stays healthy and performs.

stories.headline: Verstappen Owns Singapore, Puts Red Bull Back in the Fight
stories.body: Max Verstappen cruised to victory at Marina Bay on Sunday, his second straight win, with Leclerc second and Antonelli third. Red Bull now trails McLaren by just seven points in the constructors' standings, so that gap closed fast.

stories.headline: Antonelli One Race Away From Sealing the Title at 19
stories.body: Kimi Antonelli's podium in Singapore stretched his championship lead to 102 points, and he can mathematically clinch the title next weekend in Austin. His teammate Russell started 19th due to a power-unit penalty and still salvaged ninth, which is either impressive or a little embarrassing for everyone else.

stories.headline: Hamilton's One-Stop Gamble Backfires, Piastri Passes Him on the Last Lap
stories.body: Lewis Hamilton was left stranded on worn soft tyres late in the race after Ferrari's one-stop strategy went south, and Oscar Piastri swept past him on the final lap to take fifth. Leclerc grabbed the podium for Ferrari while Hamilton settled for sixth.

stories.headline: Barcelona Are Just Built Different Right Now
stories.body: Anthony Gordon needed 78 seconds to score his first Barcelona goal, and then Gabriel Jesus and Jules Koundé piled on in a 3–0 demolition of Getafe — eight games, eight wins, 24 points. La Liga might already be over.

stories.headline: Isco Turned Back the Clock and Betis Loved Every Second
stories.body: Real Betis hammered Osasuna 5–2 on Saturday, with Isco scoring twice and Osasuna's Ante Budimir somehow managing to score for both sides. A rough afternoon for Osasuna, to put it mildly.

stories.headline: Cole Palmer Is a Chelsea Man Until 2034 — Make That Make Sense
stories.body: Chelsea locked Palmer down with a new contract running all the way through 2034, which is either a brilliant piece of business or a very long time to be at Stamford Bridge. Probably both.

stories.headline: Sinner's Knee Hands Zverev the Year-End No. 1 Crown
stories.body: Jannik Sinner has shut down his 2026 season with knee inflammation, and the math is brutal — he'll bleed over 3,000 ranking points without defending his Paris Masters and ATP Finals titles. Alexander Zverev inherits the year-end No. 1, becoming only the second German man ever to reach the top spot after Boris Becker.

stories.headline: Djokovic Wins Title No. 102 in Beijing, Then Gets Bounced in Shanghai Two Days Later
stories.body: Novak Djokovic claimed his seventh Beijing title and 102nd career trophy after de Minaur retired hurt, going a surreal 34-0 at the China Open all-time. Hubert Hurkacz immediately brought him back to earth with a 6-4, 6-3 second-round demolition in Shanghai.

stories.headline: Alcaraz Is Back, Zheng Makes History, and a No. 1 Got Beaten by Someone Ranked Outside the Top 100
stories.body: Carlos Alcaraz ended an eight-month title drought by defending his Tokyo crown, while Zheng Qinwen became the first Chinese player to win the China Open women's title since the tournament launched in 2004. Meanwhile, Alina Charaeva became just the ninth player ever ranked outside the top 100 to defeat a world No. 1, doing it against Rybakina after dropping the first set.

stories.headline: Brennan Closes the Door in Yokohama, Pockets His Second Win of 2026
stories.body: Michael Brennan shot a final-round 68 at Yokohama Country Club to win the Baycurrent Classic at 16-under, edging Jacob Bridgeman and Keith Mitchell by one stroke. Six straight closing pars isn't exactly must-watch TV, but it got the job done.

stories.headline: Schauffele's Double Bogey on 18 Turns a Potential Win Into a Tie for Fourth
stories.body: Xander Schauffele was one shot off the lead heading to the 18th hole, then made double bogey to finish two back of Brennan at 13-under. The cruelest part of golf is that the tournament doesn't end on 17.

stories.headline: Vaughn Taylor Birdies Second Playoff Hole to Take Furyk and Friends Title
stories.body: Taylor and Alex Cejka both finished regulation at 17-under 199 at Hammock Beach Resort, traded pars on the first playoff hole, then Taylor ended it with a birdie on the second to claim his first Champions win of 2026 and $330,000.
